title: Oakland County is losing jobs. Here is why.

chapters.headline: Moving the wrong way, and moving alone
points: 648,000 Oakland County residents were employed in August 2026 — about 9,600 fewer than a year earlier
County unemployment rate 4.7%, up from 3.7% in August 2025
701,900 jobs located in the county in March 2026, down 1.7% — while Michigan, Wayne, and Macomb each edged up 0.3%
chapters.takeaway: The losses are specific — specific sectors, specific employers, specific places the work went.

chapters.headline: A concentrated decline, not a broad one
points: U-M's RSQE outlook: the county lost roughly 3,700 private-sector jobs in 2025 — against a forecast of a 3,400-job gain
Largest loss: professional, scientific & technical services, down 4,606
Health care & social assistance grew 4,655; motor vehicle manufacturing fell 1,428; RSQE projects roughly 2,600 more professional-services losses through 2028
chapters.takeaway: The single largest loss sits in the county's signature industry — the engineering and technical-services firms clustered around autos.

chapters.headline: The EV pullback, in employers' own filings
points: Webasto closed its Rochester Hills plant (244 jobs) and consolidated New Hudson (134) into Plymouth Township
Dana Thermal Products, Auburn Hills: 200 jobs, citing EV demand; Freudenberg Battery and XALT Energy: 94 combined, ceased operations
Avancez, Hazel Park: 143 after GM cancelled Factory Zero's second shift; Akebono, Farmington Hills: 48, mostly engineering roles
chapters.takeaway: The direction, repeated across independent employers with the same stated reason, is hard to argue with.

chapters.headline: Consolidation, including work that left the county
points: Fifth Third–Comerica merger (closed February 2026): 502 jobs in Farmington Hills and 234 in Auburn Hills, plus 75 Michigan branch closures
Flagstar Bank's Troy operation shed roughly 476 positions across three filings after its mortgage-servicing sale
Tribar consolidated Wixom (188) to Howell; Akasol is moving production from Hazel Park toward Seneca, South Carolina (188 jobs across two sites)
chapters.takeaway: None of these is a collapse — together they describe a footprint being consolidated elsewhere, one decision at a time.

chapters.headline: How much of the drop is real?
points: Roughly 8,000 of the 9,600-job drop appears in a single month — August 2026
Statewide, employed residents fell about 25,000 in August while the number unemployed was unchanged; participation fell to 58.8%
Initial claims were 3,739 in the week ended August 29, down 460 — and insured unemployment fell all summer, from about 51,000 to under 40,000
chapters.takeaway: Eight thousand layoffs in a month would show up in the claims data. Nothing did — the August cliff is most likely the model, not the economy.

chapters.headline: Smaller, but real
points: Health care added 4,655 jobs in 2025
Stellantis hired roughly 2,000 engineers at Auburn Hills in spring 2026 — then confirmed a white-collar hiring pause in September
Ahead: Slate Auto's 392 pledged Troy jobs over five years; Methode Electronics' headquarters move to Southfield, 90 jobs projected by 2030; GM Orion gasoline production from early 2027
chapters.takeaway: The forward announcements are pledges, not payroll — GM Orion is the largest single rebound in view.

chapters.headline: Checkpoints, not vibes
points: The September state release on October 20 will show whether August's drop holds or revises away; the county revision follows October 28
The Fifth Third layoff window completes in November
The standing rule of this series: a change is not reported without its reason — and is labeled unexplained when the evidence is not there
chapters.takeaway: We will report what the checkpoints show, either way.
